title: Consolidate overlay tokens and micro-elevation steps for dense component surfaces
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Current token set has grown organically and contains overlapping overlay colors and coarse elevation steps that cause noisy visuals in dense UIs (tables, compact cards, action lists). This ticket consolidates semantic overlay tokens and introduces a 4-step micro-elevation scale optimized for high-density surfaces. Goal: reduce visual clutter, improve contrast consistency, and provide clear migration paths for components that render many stacked surfaces.
background_and_problem_statement: We observed inconsistent overlay usage across components: some teams used opaque semantic overlays (fog-1/2) while others applied shadow-only elevations. Dense surfaces like table rows, compact controls, and small cards amplify these inconsistencies, creating perceived noise and accessibility regressions at smaller sizes. Current elevation steps (none, low, medium, high) are too coarse for micro-interactions and stacked overlays (e.g., popovers on dense tables).
proposal_summary: Introduce a consolidated set of semantic overlay tokens (surface-overlay-*/surface-muted-*) and a micro-elevation ramp (elev-micro-0..3) with corresponding shadow and alpha blends. Update token naming to be explicit about intent (overlay vs. elevation) and provide guidance and migration helpers for components: buttons, rows, tables, tooltips, popovers, and charts with overlays.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Use semantic tokens (overlay/muted/foreground) rather than surface-level color names to reduce misuse across themes.
Provide a separate micro-elevation ramp instead of reusing existing elevation steps to avoid breaking larger-card visuals.
Alpha overlays are preferred for subtle emphasis to keep chroma constant across themes; however, we will keep one solid overlay token for high-contrast modal backdrops.
Opted for 4 micro-steps to balance perceptible depth with minimal v. fine-grained complexity; adding more steps increases developer burden and choice friction.
Tradeoff: tighter visual system may require small visual tweaks on dashboards and charts — we will provide tooling and automated diff previews to accelerate review.
token_spec_high_level: surface-overlay-01..04: alpha-blend overlays with increasing opacity for localized emphasis (usable on any base surface)
surface-muted-01..02: low-contrast tints for disabled/placeholder surfaces
elev-micro-0..3: shadow + subtle lift; designed for compact stacks (row popovers, tooltips, dropdowns)
elev-standard-0..4: alias to existing system for backward compatibility
type-scale-adjustment: small-step typography tokens (type-sm/compact) for dense tables and labels
radius-compact: new radius tokens (r-compact-0..2) to unify small controls
accessibility_considerations: All overlay and elevation combinations must pass WCAG AA contrast for interactive controls; examples and automated checks will be included in the token test harness.
Provide light/dark previews and a11y delta report for each component migration PR.
Avoid relying on shadow alone to convey interactive state; pair with focus outlines or color shifts for keyboard users.
implementation_notes_for_engineering: Add new tokens to tokens.json and CSS variables: --surface-overlay-01..04, --elev-micro-0..3, --radius-compact-0..2, --type-compact-*.
Create mapping layer in token compiler so components can opt-in to :compact mode via component props or token context.
Provide a migration CLI that lists files using deprecated tokens (e.g., overlay-legacy, elev-low) and suggests replacements.
Update React component API defaults: Table.Row, Card.Compact, Button.Small should switch to compact tokens behind a feature flag.
Add visual diff snapshots to CI for affected components and a token diff page in Console for designers to review.
qa_and_acceptance_criteria: New tokens merged and available in tokens package and compiled CSS variables.
At least: Button (small/primary/secondary), Table.Row (compact), Chart.Legend overlay, Tooltip, and Popover components updated to use new tokens with visual tests passing.
Automated contrast reports show no regressions on high-impact views (dashboard, analytics table).
Migration CLI can detect >=90% of in-repo usages of legacy overlay/elevation tokens and propose mappings.
Design sign-off on Figma spec and Console token diff preview.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (token release): add tokens to tokens package, publish beta package, update Console token diff page. (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (component opt-in): update components behind feature flag; enable for internal staging and run visual diffs. (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (broad migration): flip opt-in for low-risk components and provide migration PRs for larger surfaced components (tables, charts). (3 weeks)
Phase 4 (cleanup): deprecate legacy tokens and remove after one release cycle, provide detailed changelog. (2 weeks)
Rollback: feature flags per component and token aliases to map to previous visuals if quick rollback needed.
links_and_artifacts: Confluence: Design doc - Consolidated Overlay Tokens - https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/Overlay+Consolidation
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Small contrast regressions on legacy pages — Mitigation: run tokenized contrast reports before flip and keep per-page fallbacks.
Risk: Developers misapply overlay tokens — Mitigation: document clear usage examples and add linter rules for token domains (overlay vs elevation).
Risk: Unintended performance impacts from extra CSS variables — Mitigation: compile variant bundles for compact mode and lazy-load token CSS where applicable.
notes_for_reviewers: Please review naming conventions closely — we prefer intent-first names (surface-overlay-*) over color-based names.
Check the micro-elevation visual scale at 8px, 12px, and 16px row heights to ensure perceived depth is subtle but noticeable.
Designers: confirm Figma components use updated token references (do not hardcode RGBA values).
